gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many hours of full sun each kit's own panel needs to refill an empty battery: about 3.6 h for the Reolink Argus Eco Ultra (21.6 Wh ÷ 6 W) and about 3.0 h for the Argus 4 Pro (18 Wh ÷ 6 W). The Tapo C660 and eufy S340 ship with much smaller panels, 2.5 W and 2.2 W.
standout_why: I checked the two pages ChatGPT cited. rottenwifi.com/best-solar-powered-home-security-cameras-for-2026 gives the Argus 4 Pro's 5,000 mAh battery and 6 W panel but no wattage for the S340 or the Tapo panels. It does not compute Wh, refill hours or daily energy. reolink.com/blog/solar-powered-security-cameras-buying-guide gives the Eco Ultra's 21.6 Wh battery and the Argus 4 Pro's 5,000 mAh battery and 6 W panel, but no refill time and no comparison with other brands. Neither page sets battery size against panel watts for the four cameras ChatGPT showed, and neither says that the eufy and Tapo panels have 37–42% of the Reolink panel's rating. I did not open the uncited results.
decides: This supports the Reolink kits for shaded yards and winter. Their 6 W panels can refill a fully drained battery in one good sunny day (about 3–3.6 h at full rated output). The Tapo C660 (2.5 W) and eufy S340 (2.2 W) collect less than half as much energy per sun-hour. Tapo's own claim implies a daily budget of under 1.9 Wh, which leaves little spare for recovering after cloudy spells. Meanwhile eufy's own store price for the S340 ($219.99) is $60 above the $159.99 ChatGPT showed.

findings.label: Battery energy
findings.note: Maker page says '21.6Wh rechargeable battery', weight 431 g with battery, and 'about 4 months per charge' (also '1 to 4 months') with no stated test conditions. The panel is sold separately or in a '1 Camera + 1 Solar Panel' bundle. This page does not give the panel's wattage.

findings.label: Full-sun hours to refill from empty with Solar Panel 2
findings.source_title: Reolink blog: Argus 4 Pro vs Argus 4
findings.note: 21.6 Wh ÷ 6 W = 3.6 h. The Solar Panel 2 is rated 6 W on this Reolink page. This assumes the bundled panel is the Solar Panel 2 and that it gives full rated output at 1000 W/m²; charging losses make the real time longer.

findings.label: Battery energy
findings.source_title: Reolink blog: Argus 4 Pro vs Argus 4
findings.note: The page says the Pro uses a '5000mAh (same cell as Argus 4)' and lists the Argus 4 as '5000mAh, 18Wh'. The Pro's 18 Wh therefore comes from Reolink's same-cell statement.

findings.label: Full-sun hours to refill from empty with Solar Panel 2
findings.note: 18 Wh ÷ 6 W = 3.0 h. The maker spec lists 'Reolink Solar Panel 2 (6W)'. This is an ideal figure before charging losses.

findings.label: Average daily energy at Reolink's 300 s/day duty
findings.note: 18 Wh ÷ 60 days = 0.3 Wh/day, using the FAQ's 'about 2 months per charge' at 300 s of recording per day. At the panel's 6 W rating that is 0.3 ÷ 6 × 60 = 3 min of full sun per day.

findings.label: Panel rating
findings.note: Maker spec: 'Solar Panel Max Charging Power: 2.5 W' (Tapo A201). That is 2.5 ÷ 6 = 42% of the Reolink Solar Panel 2's rating.

findings.label: Daily energy budget implied by Tapo's 45-minute claim
findings.note: 0.75 h × 2.5 W = 1.875 Wh. Tapo says 45 minutes of direct sun at 1000 W/m², 25 °C, AM1.5 'powers the Tapo C660 camera for a full day' with up to 100 events per day. This is the most the panel can deliver in that time, so it is an upper bound on daily use.
